title: add NVTX ranges and microbench instrumentation for runtime kernels and continuous batching
author: Priya Nair
description: Add NVTX scopes and lightweight counters around critical runtime codepaths (kernel launch, scheduler, KV cache lookup/commit, and continuous batching hot loops), plus a small microbenchmark harness and Prometheus exports to validate end-to-end regression detection. Motivation: recent production investigations showed opaque tail latency spikes that trace back to kernel scheduling and batching inefficiencies; this PR surfaces precise timing and event counts to make root-cause analysis reproducible and to feed perf dashboards. Changes include NVTX ranges around attention/softmax/kernel entry/exit, an opt-in microbench binary (tools/microbench) that exercises batching and KV cache patterns with deterministic workloads, a thin metrics adapter that exposes counters (kv_hit, kv_miss, batch_size_histogram, kernel_duration_ms) to our metrics pipeline, and a Grafana dashboard template for kernel and batching heatmaps. The description below contains a short checklist of work items included.
commits_summary: 6 commits: initial NVTX wrappers and macros; instrument attention and matmul kernels; add KV cache hit/miss counters and histograms; microbench harness for batching and KV patterns; prometheus adapter and dashboard JSON; unit tests and small runtime refactors to make instrumentation opt-in and low overhead.
review_conversation: Oliver Hart: Appreciate the NVTX hygiene. Can you confirm the overhead numbers on a p3dn-24? We need <=1% overhead at typical QPS.

Author (Priya): Measured with microbench at 8 concurrent streams on p3dn-24: NVTX ranges add ~0.6% median overhead, 0.9% tail. Counters are atomics with cacheline padding; microbench shows <0.5% overhead for counters enabled. Added numbers to PR description and a standalone perf note in tools/microbench/README.md.

Daniel Kim: Suggest we gate NVTX behind a runtime flag to avoid shipping NVTX in our release builds where customers might have different tooling. Also request a small unit test to validate the kv_hit/kv_miss increment path.
Author (Priya): NVTX and counters are behind runtime config flags (instrumentation.enabled and instrumentation.nvtx). Added a unit test for KV counter paths and updated the config docs.
Sofia Alvarez: I reran the CI perf check and saw a regression in the scheduler latency histogram on the first run; second run passed. Please mention flakiness and add a retry in the perf CI job.
Author (Priya): Added a retry wrapper to the perf job and a comment in CI config referencing ENG-4870. Also included a note about environmental noise in the microbench README. Ready for squash-merge.
Oliver Hart: Approve after telemetry gating and test additions. LGTM.
release_notes: Added runtime NVTX ranges for critical kernels (attention, matmul) to aid profiling and tracing.
Introduced lightweight KV cache counters (kv_hit, kv_miss) and batching histograms to help diagnose cache and batching effectiveness.
Added microbench harness (tools/microbench) to reproduce batching/KV patterns and generate stable baselines for perf regression detection.
Exported new instrumentation metrics to Prometheus and included Grafana dashboard template for kernel and batching heatmaps.
Instrumentation is opt-in and gated by configuration flags; defaults remain disabled in release builds to avoid overhead.
